How to use this sheet

  1. Print the PDF and keep it near your plant shelf or posted on the fridge.
  2. Fill in each plant, its location and a starting watering interval. Use the houseplant watering calculator linked below to plan upcoming dates.
  3. After you water a plant, update the Last watered date and calculate Next due by adding the watering interval.
  4. Use the Soil / light column for quick care notes — succulent mix, indirect light, bottom-watering only — so anyone watering your plants has the key info.
  5. Review the sheet regularly. Treat Next due as a reminder to check soil against that plant’s needs; if watering can wait, update the date after you actually water.

Questions

Is this plant watering schedule printable free?

Yes. Download the one-page PDF and print it without signup or email.

How do I know how often to water houseplants?

Use a plant-specific interval as a starting point and check soil moisture before watering. Pot size, soil, light and season change how quickly a plant dries. The linked houseplant watering calculator helps plan dates; it does not measure moisture.

Is this an indoor plant moisture level chart PDF?

This PDF is a watering log, not a moisture meter chart. Record your own soil observations in the care notes; it does not provide numerical moisture targets.

Can I use it as a plant watering calendar?

Yes. Record each plant’s last watered and next due dates. For a weekly checklist, use the related plant watering calendar; for a sitter, use the vacation plant watering plan.
